correctness.rationale: Scaling of independent renewed excursions gives A=T^(1+beta/2)Y, with Y=sqrt(2K) integral_0^1 |B(u^beta)|du. Gaussian signed-area lower tail and Borell supremum upper tail give log P(Y>y) ~ -y²/(2v), v=4K/((beta+1)(beta+2)); positivity of covariance ensures this is maximal variance. Integrating over Exp(r) durations at t=x^[2/(beta+3)]u yields strict convex cost h(u)=ru+(2v u^(beta+2))^-1. Its unique minimum gives sharp cycle tail and the conditional winning-duration localization via constrained Laplace bounds. Independence of cycle marks gives maxima; exponential order statistics give the longest interval, and a renewal-count sandwich covers physical time without including the final incomplete interval. Independent exact kernel integration and saddle algebra checked beta=1/2,1,3/2, including Brownian 3/8 and duration 3/4. The finite checks do not prove the large-deviation limits; the Gaussian concentration and localized saddle argument do.
